title: Certificate Issuance and Reissue Conditions
content:
Operating terms agreed with the partner certificate authority for SSL/TLS Certificates, governing when a certificate may be issued under a subscription, how long each certificate is valid, and the terms of reissues and duplicates.

## 1. Status of the subscription

A certificate may be issued only while the subscription status is pending validation or active. The status is the one shown on the subscription record for that subscription reference number. A subscription that is expired, revoked or cancelled has no certificate issued under it.

## 2. Validity of each certificate

Each certificate is valid until the earlier of its issue date plus the product's longest certificate validity in days and the subscription end date. From 15 March 2027 the product's longest certificate validity from that date replaces the earlier figure. The validity of a certificate never runs beyond the subscription end date.

## 3. Freshness of validation at issuance

3.1 A certificate may be issued only on or before the date domain control was last validated plus the product's domain validation reuse period in days.

3.2 An OV or EV certificate may be issued only on or before the date organisation validation last completed plus the product's organisation validation reuse period in days.

3.3 Each validity window adds whole calendar days to the validation date, counting the day after it as day 1, and the last day is included; outside it validation must be repeated first. Both dates are read from the subscription record, never from the customer's account of when validation was done.

*Boundary pair (hypothetical).* With domain control last validated on 10 January 2032 and a reuse period of 200 days, day 1 is 11 January 2032 and day 200 is 28 July 2032. A certificate may be issued on 28 July 2032, the last day included; on 29 July 2032 the window has passed and domain control must be validated again before issuance.

3.4 Where the product voids earlier domain validation on a change of registrant, and the covered Harborline domain registration shows a last registrant change date later than the date domain control was last validated, domain control must be validated again before any issuance.

## 4. Reissues and duplicates

- Reissues cost the product's reissue fee.
- Reissues are limited to the product's largest number of reissues per certificate in a trailing 30 days. The trailing 30 days are the 30 calendar days ending today, today included, and the count is the number of issuances of kind reissue for that certificate whose moment of issuance falls in them.
- Duplicates for other servers are free where the product allows duplicate certificates.

*Illustration (hypothetical).* On 8 March 2034 the trailing 30 days run from 7 February 2034 to 8 March 2034, both included; a reissue recorded on 6 February 2034 no longer counts, one recorded on 7 February 2034 still does.

## 5. Automatic reissue

Where validation can complete automatically, the next certificate of the subscription is issued the product's automatic-reissue lead time in days before the current certificate expires; otherwise the customer is reminded to reissue.
